parsed.explanation: The combined regime is high-risk. Federal passport/visa screening demands binary markers; mismatches can cause refusal, detention/stranding, and possible lifetime fraud findings. Federal facilities and many state facilities exclude trans use; one documented trespass arrest with men’s-ward detention shows criminal exposure. Federal/immigration custody has documented forced labour and sexual abuse, outweighing state court-mandated care. A protective state adds shield laws, gender-affirming insurance and prison-care orders, helping adults seeking care and maybe minors locally, but it cannot preempt entry screening, federal facilities, federal custody or border fraud investigations. For an adult alone, federal exposure dominates; for a minor with guardian, care is safer locally but border scrutiny and family outing risk remain. Court contests create uncertainty.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal visa/passport screening requires binary sex markers; mismatch, nonbinary markers, or evidence of transition can cause refusals, additional evidence, detention/stranding, and possible lifetime immigration-fraud finding.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiration; some orders are challenged and legal-aid FAQ advises travelers.
entry_documents.interaction: State shield laws do not preempt federal passport/visa/entry screening or fraud adjudication.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections/immigration custody documented forced labour, sexual abuse, denial of care, solitary, and birth-sex disciplinary placement; national custody rules are hostile to gender identity.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State prisons are under court orders to provide gender-affirming care, including surgery.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State prison protections do not cover federal or immigration custody or border investigations.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive bars congruent use in government-funded facilities; many states restrict schools/public buildings and some criminalize use; a documented arrest led to men’s-ward detention.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Protective-state status suggests fewer local restrictions, but dossier does not document a visitor-facing facility protection.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal and state facility rules operate together; local shields do not override federal facilities.

care_services.exposure: National funding, reimbursement and school-care hostility restrict trans care, especially for minors, and federal facilities may deny care.
care_services.protection: State has comprehensive gender-affirming insurance and shield laws against out-of-state action; prison-care court orders.
care_services.interaction: Shield helps state-provided care but not border entry, federal custody, or federal facilities; enforcement record unknown.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism and official rhetoric frame radical transgender advocacy as hostile; entry screening treats sex doubt/fraud as grounds; restrictive states enable police arrests for facilities.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime law, employment-discrimination precedent, and partial state anti-discrimination; some lawsuits contest policies.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Protective-state enforcement may help locally; federal screening/fraud and hostile state policing remain.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minors’ care/social transition targeted by national rules; document mismatch can out child and parent, trigger visa refusals, stranding, or family investigations.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield/insurance may protect local care and refuge, but applicability to minors and ballot outcome are uncertain.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family travel increases scrutiny; federal border/funding rules still reach minors despite state protections.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence rate documented; hostile official climate and facility-criminal laws can bring police into encounters, with documented arrest risk.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime law and protective-state institutions may support reporting; 22 states plus capital district have anti-discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Response varies sharply by jurisdiction; in protective state recourse may work, elsewhere not.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Many restrictive rules remain operative despite litigation; passport/visa fraud findings, facility arrests, and federal custody lack fast, traveler-facing remedy.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined some orders; ACLU suit, state shield laws and prison-care rulings may create relief.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are slow, jurisdiction-dependent, and cannot cure border refusal or federal custody harm.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher severity because documented federal/immigration custody abuse and possible permanent fraud, but protective-state shield laws make it less universally restrictive than Vellandra’s entry register.

Comparable universal documentary exposure; lower than Drellia because no mandatory local police/hotel database registration is documented, and care protections exist; still high due entry fraud and custody.

Lower than Vellmaris because this jurisdiction has operative federal binary-document screening, criminalizable facility bans, and severe federal custody, not merely brief provincial questioning with reliable release.

parsed.synthesis: National binary-document, entry-fraud, and federal-facility rules operate everywhere; protective-state shield laws and insurance/care orders mitigate only state-local care and corrections. The traveller’s border passage is the highest-probability exposure: document mismatch can escalate to refusal, stranding, and possible permanent fraud. If removed or detained, federal/immigration custody adds severe abuse. In the protective state, an adult or family seeking care has meaningful operational shelter, but only after lawful entry and not against federal screening/federal facilities. Minors gain local care protection while still exposed to marker mismatch and family outing; ballot initiatives make local posture uncertain.
